name: CarParts.com, Inc.

profile.description: Online-only retailer of aftermarket collision, engine and performance auto parts and accessories for consumers and professional installers.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track record 1: online-only model and own-brand parts, but no recent transformative launch. AI 2: third-generation AI search matches VINs to compatibility data at 98% accuracy and an AI shopping assistant has launched [2]. Market share 1: meaningful but shrinking (TTM revenue $515.8M, -10.7%) [1]. Pipeline 0: no named next-gen items. R&D 0: not disclosed.

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission floor 2: clear online auto-parts access aim, not distinctive. Community, retention and insider buying not evidenced; Glassdoor's 3.9 rating is not scored [2]. Scored 0 on adds.

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: Liquidity floor triggered: about 44,452 shares x $8.52 is roughly $0.38M daily, below $1M, so Infrastructure is 0 regardless of metrics (D/E 90%, ROE -46%, margin -5.4%, revenue -10.7%) [1].

ai_resilience.label: HIGH RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: E-commerce parts retail is exposed to AI shopping agents and marketplace intermediaries such as Amazon, and the company's own 10-Q lists AI as an operational, competitive and reputational risk [2]. Physical fulfillment and VIN-fitment data provide partial defense. AI tools are internal, with no AI revenue, so tiebreaker is 0.

infinite_game.summary: Turnaround-stage retailer focusing on profitability over growth; a purpose exists but strategy responds to quarterly results.

just_cause.analysis: Making parts accessible online is service-oriented but shallow and not a distinctive cause [2].

trusting_teams.analysis: CEO David Meniane has 83% approval on Glassdoor and a people-first reputation, but sentiment is average (3.9/5) [2].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Competitive framing is about share against Amazon and brick-and-mortar chains; no worthy-rival language.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Shift from growth-at-all-costs to profit-focused marketing rationalization is a meaningful but incremental pivot [1].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Cutting marketing spend to reach positive adjusted EBITDA ($585K in Q1 2026) sacrifices revenue, which is a costly but sensible choice [1].

investment_thesis: Q1 2026 produced the first positive adjusted EBITDA since Q1 2024 ($585K, a swing of nearly $7M) and Q2 net loss narrowed to $3.2M as marketing spend was rationalized [1]. AI-driven search at 98% fitment accuracy supports conversion.
thesis_continued: Revenue is falling 10% (Q2 $135.6M), net margin is -5.4%, ROE is -46%, and the $69M market cap with only 44K shares of daily volume fails the IOWN liquidity floor [1]. Amazon and AI shopping agents pressure a rationalized marketing model [2].
key_catalysts: Sustained positive adjusted EBITDA as marketing efficiency improves
Stabilization of revenue after marketing rationalization
AI search and assistant lifting conversion
key_risks: Illiquidity and competition from Amazon and AI shopping agents
